name: Maths: Applications & Interpretation
blurb: Number, functions, geometry, statistics and calculus for modelling the real world, with technology

units.title: Number and algebra
units.blurb: Standard form, sequences, finance, logarithms; HL: complex numbers and matrices.

units.title: Functions
units.blurb: Lines, functions and modelling; HL: transformations, further models and linearising data.

units.title: Geometry and trigonometry
units.blurb: 3D shapes, triangle trigonometry and Voronoi diagrams; HL: vectors, matrix transformations and graph theory.

units.title: Statistics and probability
units.blurb: Data, regression, probability distributions and hypothesis tests; HL: confidence intervals, Poisson and Markov chains.

units.title: Calculus
units.blurb: Derivatives, optimisation and integration; HL: further calculus, kinematics and differential equations.

components.name: Paper 3
components.detail: Two compulsory extended problem-solving questions, technology required

ia.name: Mathematical exploration

criteria.name: Presentation
look: A clear aim stated early and a rationale for why the topic was chosen
A logical structure: introduction, body developed in coherent steps, conclusion that returns to the aim
Concise writing that a peer could follow without re-reading; no padding or irrelevant material
Graphs, tables and diagrams placed where they are discussed, not dumped in an appendix

criteria.name: Mathematical communication
look: Correct notation, symbols and terminology throughout (no calculator syntax such as x^2 or *)
Key variables and terms defined before they are used
Multiple forms of representation (formulae, graphs, tables, diagrams) chosen to suit the mathematics
Graphs with labelled axes, scales and units; tables with headings

criteria.name: Personal engagement
look: Evidence that you drove the exploration: your own question, data, model or approach
Thinking independently or creatively rather than reproducing a textbook example
Asking your own follow-up questions and testing your own ideas

criteria.name: Reflection
look: Critical reflection throughout, not just a paragraph at the end
Discussion of the meaning, limitations and implications of each result
Considering the reasonableness of assumptions and how results could be improved or extended

criteria.name: Use of mathematics
look: Mathematics relevant to the aim and at a level commensurate with the course (SL or HL)
Correct mathematics: calculations, algebra and technology output are accurate
Thorough understanding shown by explaining why methods work, not only applying them
HL only: sophistication and rigour in the mathematics used

checklist: The aim is stated in the introduction and answered in the conclusion
Length is within 12–20 pages, with no appendix holding essential work
Every variable is defined, with units, before it is used
No calculator notation: x², not x^2; ×, not *
Every graph has a title, labelled axes, scales and units
Technology output is interpreted in words, not just pasted in
At least one calculation per method is shown by hand or explained step by step
Assumptions of each model are stated and their effect discussed
Reflection appears throughout, including limitations and possible extensions
Data sources and all references are cited consistently
The mathematics is at least at the level of your course (SL or HL)
A classmate could read it and follow the argument without your help

examTips: Give final answers to 3 significant figures unless told otherwise, and keep full calculator accuracy in intermediate steps.
Write down what you enter into your GDC (e.g. the equation solved or the regression type chosen); a bare answer that is wrong earns no method marks.
Interpret answers in context with units: "the model predicts 4.2 thousand users after 6 months" beats "y = 4.2".
For hypothesis tests, state H₀ and H₁ in context, quote the p-value or test statistic, compare with the significance level, and conclude in words.
Comment on validity: extrapolating a regression line or model far outside the data range is unreliable, and examiners reward saying so.
